admission.justification: Two cases prove the admitted unconfigured state is named and reaches no host; a blanket refusal would break every fresh build, and an unnamed admission would hide the state.

applicability: A request whose sandbox records no host while the build resolves none under the sandbox environment; the fresh build's asset bootstrap is the occasion this exists for.
conditions: The build resolves no Paseo runtime under the sandbox environment.
The sandbox records no host of its own.
exclusions: Once a host is recorded or resolved, the host comparison of the preceding clause applies.
No call that needs a host can succeed in this state.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_pnt_sandbox.py::test_a_sandbox_that_records_no_host_yet_is_admitted_only_without_one and ::test_a_host_outside_the_sandbox_refuses_in_the_unconfigured_phase; the real unconfigured run in the freeze report §Proof — the unconfigured state (evidence/real-unconfigured-report.json, role_start refused with no-paseo-runtime-configured)

statement: In a fresh build, where no Paseo runtime is configured at all, the request is admitted and its report says no host is configured; in that state no call reaches any Paseo home or address outside the sandbox, the developer's defaults and a default home under HOME included.
